name: product-demo
title: Product demo
summary: A 30-to-120-second walkthrough of the real product, built from real app captures: context, the task, the walkthrough, the result.
use_when: The product itself is the story and the viewer should see it working, exactly as it ships.

9:16.note: For phone apps, the vertical cut shows the app at its own shape.

beats.name: context
beats.job: Who this is for and the moment they reach for the product.

beats.name: task
beats.job: The one job the viewer wants done.

beats.name: walkthrough
beats.job: The job done in the real product, each tap landing on the word that names it.

beats.name: result
beats.job: What the viewer has at the end.

rules: Show only what ships today: nothing unbuilt, stubbed or switched off is ever shown working.
A seeded demo account and sample data, labelled as sample data; never a real customer's data.
One set of numbers across every shot: the same sample company everywhere.

capture.source: slate capture ios (the Simulator, with status-bar overrides, a seeded demo account and a pinned build) or slate capture web (through Aside at a fixed viewport)
capture.principle: Capture for truth and speed; rebuild in code when a shot needs camera moves, restaging, motion blur or exact type.
rules: Captures are conformed to the film's frame rate as image sequences and beat-mapped, so taps land on voice words and make their sounds.
A rebuilt shot matches the real screen pixel for pixel before it moves.

captions.position: below the product, clear of the app's own controls
captions.note: Demos often play muted on sites and in feeds, so captions are burned in; the vertical cut uses shorter lines.

budget.note: No Higgsfield budget: generation is off, because the product's truth comes from captures. If the requester turns generation on for a scene the product can't show, raise the budget with them (up to the explainer family's $60).
